svg.title: Ryde Resolve: architecture and information flows
svg.desc: A run starts from the Input, in three groups: case data (simulated: GPS and Telemetry Data, checked for route, stops, arrival, time against the estimate and the rider's location; Chat and Communication Logs, read for sentiment and threats; Payment and Fare Data, checked for breakdown, surge and promo; Historical Behavior Profiles, checked for disputes, ratings and account age; the dispute and statements; photos and receipts), rules and precedents, and external sources queried during the run to add to the case data. Preparing the case runs a safety screen (a code text check), the Fraud and Bad-Faith Detection Agent (our record check in code; matches go to a person) and a cleaning intake check. The live worker runs Image Analysis (Multi-Modal), then the agents, each in a fresh Tencent CodeBuddy session every time it takes its turn: the Evidence Collection Agent, which also reads each chat message for sentiment, agreements, disagreements and threats (an AI text check; a threat or abusive message holds the run for a person), the Policy and Precedent Agent, the Rider and Driver Advocate Agents, and the Arbitrator (the handbook's Judge Agent). Every agent step, tool call and hand-off is shown live, in a log no agent can change. Release checks apply the Escalation Protocol (safety, a remedy over S$50 (over S$200 for a vomit cleaning payment), or low confidence: sent to a person) and the SLA and Routing Manager. The Output is either a decision with notices prepared for the rider and driver (a code text check holds back a notice that reveals the other side's details or promises a payment), or the case sent to a person. The Learning Feedback Loop turns a person's ruling, privacy-checked, into a past ruling. A side panel lists the stack and architecture, then notes on operators, prompts, fair hearing, citations, the audit trail, the confidence score, response times and results.
